excerpt_i18n.en: Over the past six years, domestic GPU companies have ridden the AI wave, with valuations constantly refreshed, while DPU has been overlooked. This does not align with industry reality. After Nvidia acquired Mellanox in 2020, it clearly defined its "GPU+CPU+DPU" three-chip strategy. In recent years, Nvidia has continued to strengthen its networking capabilities. When Jensen Huang showcased the "six-chip combination" at CES 2026, four of the chips were network-related. An increasingly clear trend is emerging: the bottleneck in AI infrastructure is shifting from computing power itself to networking and scheduling. Especially with the arrival of the Agent era, AI systems are transitioning from training to high-frequency inference and continuous operation, making GPU utilization increasingly dependent on network efficiency. The DPU has also evolved from an optional component in data centers to a key player in AI infrastructure. However, a thought-provoking question remains: since Nvidia had already bet on DPU, why did the entire industry still underestimate DPU over the past six years? It wasn't until the Shenzhen Stock Exchange accepted the IPO filing of Cloud Leopard Smart, the first domestic DPU company, and the prospectus was laid before everyone, that the market began to realize that a full-featured DPU capable of supporting low latency, high bandwidth, and high-performance data scheduling might be the most overlooked piece of the AI infrastructure puzzle. A large-chip track undervalued for six years. Over the past few years, the focus of competition in the AI industry has always been on GPU. Larger model parameters, stronger single-card performance, and more expensive HBM have almost captured the entire industry's attention.
excerpt_i18n.es: Durante los últimos seis años, las empresas nacionales de GPU han aprovechado la ola de la IA, con valoraciones que se actualizan constantemente, mientras que las DPU han sido ignoradas.
